correctness.rationale: For a simple CCW polygon with a marked point strictly in its kernel, all oriented edge determinants are positive and its boundary has winding one. Hence adjacent angular changes uniquely equal arccos of normalized edge Gram data in (0,pi) and sum to 2pi. Cumulative angles yield every missing Gram entry, proving orthogonal uniqueness and the metric symmetry assertion. The 792-case, 22932-dihedral diagnostic corroborates but does not replace this all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The surviving contribution is exact Gram completion for *nonconvex* star-shaped polygonal cycles under a strict-kernel hypothesis, not the convex polygon result. Winter 2023 reconstruction, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.10, already covers any two combinatorially equivalent convex polygons, but assumes convex polytopes and therefore does not imply the asserted nonconvex reconstruction. Winter 2021 discusses metric coloring and explicitly asks for nonconvex geometric criteria. published-finding corpus and owned-current-week searches found no equivalent star-shaped polygon reconstruction. The generic global rigidity of wheel graphs does not establish arbitrary nongeneric placement rigidity.

value.rationale: The precise geometric gap is nonconvex metric reconstruction: general embedded cycles admit hidden angle-branch changes, whereas a natural infinite family of concave simple polygons with a strict star-center has an explicit global Gram completion and full colored-symmetry rigidity. This is a structural sufficient criterion extending convex-polytope reconstruction to a genuinely nonconvex class, demonstrated by an alternating-radius concave hexagon. The exact O(n^2) completion is usable without genericity, and the restricted hypothesis and literature coverage are explicitly reported.
